intent: I hate the upgrade treadmill. I want to buy one phone now and still be happily using it in 2031. What actually ends a phone's life? Is it the battery wearing out, the screen burning in, the software going stale, or just the charging port getting flaky? Some of that sounds fixable and some doesn't. I'd like to understand which failure modes are physics and which are policy, hear from people who genuinely kept a phone five-plus years about what gave out first, and then get your pick for the model, plus the case and charging habits, that make the long haul realistic.

intent_v1_legacy: I keep hearing that most of the universe is this invisible 'dark matter' nobody can actually see, and honestly it smells like a fudge factor physicists invented to make their sums work. But apparently there's real evidence. Can you walk me through the actual observations that convince astronomers something unseen is out there, the spinning of galaxies, that Bullet Cluster thing people bring up, the bending of light, and so on? For each one, what does it tell us about what dark matter is? And where does the MOND alternative fit, is it a serious rival or basically finished? I want to see which lines are rock solid versus still fought over.
